1525: It shall be a nuisance per se for the owner or occupant of any lot, tract or parcel of land or premises in the city to permit the growth thereon of weeds or vegetative undergrowth of a nature or density so as to violate the provisions of this article or so as to endanger the public health, safety or welfare, or so as to block public roads, streets, alleys or sidewalks.
1526: It shall be the duty of the city police chief or designee to notify, in writing, the owner or occupant of any premises upon which weeds or other prohibited flora permitted to grow in violation of the provisions of this article that such growths must be removed, cut or destroyed within ten days from the date of such notice. Notice shall be by registered mail, addressed to said owner or occupant, at his last known address, and by posting on the subject property. Notice shall be complete upon posting.
1527: Upon the failure, neglect, or refusal of any owner or occupant so notified to remove, cut, or destroy such weeds or other unsightly growths within the designated time period, the appropriate city departments and employees are authorized and empowered to provide for the removal, cutting, or destroying of such growths by or for the city.
1528: The actual cost of such weed removal shall be assessed against the property owner upon whose premises the work is done and a statement of the sums due shall be provided to the owner in the same manner as provided for notices to remove. In the event the bill for such charges remains unpaid ten days after it has been rendered, shall become a lien upon the premises enforceable in the same manner as provided for the collection of unpaid taxes.
1532:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Crown spread means the distance measured across the greatest diameter of a plant.
Park tree means either evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs located on land designated as public park land. Public park land shall be land owned or leased by the city and used for public park purposes.
Shade tree means any self-supporting woody plant of a species that is normally well-shaped, well-branched and well-foliated which normally grows to an overall height of at least 35 feet and normally develops an average mature crown spread greater than 30 feet.
Small tree means either evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs, which do not normally exceed 12 feet in height at maturity. No tree which exceeds 12 feet in height shall be classified as a small tree.
Street tree means either evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs located on land lying within the public right-of-way on either side of all public streets, roads, avenues or ways within the city.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § V(a)—(c))
1533:
The city tree board shall develop and maintain a list of species of street, park, shade and small trees which said tree board recommends for the planting of new trees within the city.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § V(d))
1534:
(a) Any person, legal or natural, found guilty of violation any provision of this article shall be subject to penalties as provided in section 1-18.
(b) Action pursuant to any provision of this article shall not be a bar to the enforcement of this article by injunction or other appropriate remedy, and the city, acting by and through the city building inspector, or other duly authorized individual, shall have the power to institute and maintain in the name of the city any and all such enforcement proceedings.
(c) Nothing in this article shall be construed to abridge, limit, or otherwise impair the right of any person to institute and maintain any action or other appropriate proceeding for damages or other relief on account of injuries to persons or property.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § XIII)
1537:
There is hereby created and established a city tree board, which shall consist of five members, who shall be residents of the city, and who shall be appointed by the mayor and city council.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § I)
1538:
The term of office for each the members of the city tree board shall be one year. In the event that a vacancy shall occur during the term of any member of said board, the mayor and council shall appoint a successor to fill the unexpired portion of the term of such member.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § II)
1539:
Members of the tree board shall serve without compensation, except for such per-meeting stipends as may be authorized by the mayor and city council.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § III)
1540:
(a) It shall be the responsibility of the tree board to study and investigate the care, preservation, pruning, planting, replanting, removal and/or disposition of trees and shrubs in parks, along public streets and in other public areas, and to periodically report such studies and investigations to the mayor and city council. The tree board, when requested by the mayor and city council, shall consider, investigate, make findings, report and recommend upon any specific matter or question coming within the scope of its work. All such studies, investigations, considerations, findings, reports and/or recommendations shall be advisory only. The mayor and council shall designate the chairman of said tree board. The tree board shall:
(1) By majority vote elect all other officers it deems necessary and appropriate;
(2) By majority vote adopt such rules governing the conduct of its meetings which are not contrary to law; and
(3) Keep minutes of its meetings.
(b) A majority of the members shall be a quorum for the transaction of business.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § IV)
1541:
It shall be unlawful for any person to prevent, delay or interfere with the city tree board, or any of its members and/or agents, while engaged in conducting the activities of authorized by this division.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § XII)
1544:
No tree (whether street tree, park tree, shade tree or small tree) shall be planted or otherwise located closer than 20 feet from the intersection of any public street with another public street or with a designated private street, as measured from point of intersection of the nearest paved surfaces of such streets. However, shrubs of less than three feet in height are allowed to be located not less than four feet from such intersections. No tree (whether street tree, park tree, shade tree or small tree) shall be planted or otherwise located closer than ten feet from any fire hydrant. This section shall apply only to the planting and/or location of new trees and shall not be interpreted to require the removal of trees in the ground on the date of adoption of the ordinance from which this division is derived. This section shall not apply to the central business district of the city.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § VI)
1545:
No tree, other than a tree meeting the definition of a small tree as set forth in this division, shall be planted or located under or within ten lateral feet of any overhead utility wire, or over or within five lateral feet of any underground water line, sewer line, power line, or other utility. This section shall apply only to the planting or location of new trees and shall not be interpreted to require the removal of trees in the ground on the date of adoption of the ordinance from which this division is derived.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § VII)
1546:
(a) The city shall have the right, power and authority to plant, prune, maintain and remove trees, plants and shrubs within the boundaries and rights-of-way of the streets, alleys, avenues, lanes, squares, and public grounds of the city, as may be necessary to insure public safely and to preserve or enhance the symmetry and beauty of such streets, alleys, avenues, lanes, squares, and public grounds of the city.
(b) The city shall have the right, power and authority to remove, or cause or order to be removed, any tree or part thereof within the boundaries and rights-of-way of the streets, alleys, avenues, lanes, squares, and public grounds of the city, which tree or any part thereof:
(1) Is in an unsafe condition;
(2) By reason of its nature or condition, is injurious to sewers, electrical power lines, gas lines, water lines, or other public improvements and/or the structural integrity of any public street or sidewalk; and/or
(3) Is infected with any injurious fungus, insect or other pest.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § VIII)
1547:
It shall be unlawful, as a normal practice, for any person or city department to top any street tree, park tree, or other tree on public property. Topping is defined as the severe cutting back of limbs to stubs larger than three inches in diameter within the tree's crown to such a degree so as to remove the normal canopy and disfigure the tree. Trees severely damaged by storms or other causes or certain trees under utility wires where other pruning practices are impractical shall be exempted from this section.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § IX)
1548:
Every owner of any tree overhanging any public street or right-of-way within the city shall prune the branches of such tree so that such branches shall not obstruct the light from any streetlamp or obstruct the view of any street intersection and so that there shall be a clear space of eight feet above the surface of the street or sidewalk. Said owners shall remove all dead, diseased or dangerous trees, or broken or decayed limbs, which constitute a menace to the safety of the public. The city shall have the right to prune any tree or shrub on private property when it interferes with the proper spread of lights along the street from a streetlight or interferes with the visibility of any traffic control device or sign.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § X)
1549:
(a) The city shall have the right, power and authority to cause the removal of any dead or diseased tree located on private property within the city, when such tree:
(1) Constitutes a hazard to life;
(2) Constitutes a hazard to property; and/or
(3) Harbors insects or disease which constitute a potential threat to other trees within the city. Diseased or dangerous trees constitute nuisances per se.
(b) The city shall have the right, power and authority to take such action immediately in those instances which present a clear and immediate danger of substantial harm to persons and/or property. In all other instances, the city may initiate action to have such tree removed under the applicable provisions of the nuisance provisions of article IV of chapter 36, as now or hereafter amended.
(Ord. of 12-10-2003, § XI)
1550: The city has adopted, as stated in chapter 64, Standard Development Specifications, April 2002, that include specifications with regard to tree and shrub buffers and other landscaping requirements. The adopted specifications shall be applicable to vegetation within the city to the extent set forth therein. A copy of the adopted specifications are available in the office of the city clerk.

1556:
It is the purpose of this article to protect the public health, welfare and safety of its citizens through the proper licensing of taxi businesses and require that those persons operating taxicabs do so in a safe, fair and efficient manner. To provide for application requirements, licensing, required issuance of insurance, permits, permit fees, fines and penalties, appeal of suspension or permit denial and severability.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1557:
The following words, terms, or phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings given in this section.
Certificate means a certificate of public convenience and necessity issued by the city clerk authorizing the holder to conduct a taxicab business in the city.
City means City of Cleveland, Georgia.
Holder means a person to whom a certificate of public convenience and necessity has been issued.
Taxicab means any vehicle designed and used for the purpose of transporting less than 15 passengers for consideration or charges which are determined by agreement, contract, mileage, or length of time, not operating from a fixed terminal on a fixed route.
Taxi operator's permit means the written permission, granted by the city, to a person to operate a taxicab on the streets of the city.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1558:
No person shall do business or permit a taxicab owned or controlled by him/her to do business in the city without first having obtained a certificate of public convenience.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1559:
An application for a certificate of public convenience shall be filed with the city clerk on forms provided by the city. The applicant is required to submit to a criminal history background check. The applicant must:
(1) Be at least 21 years of age.
(2) Be a citizen of the United States, an alien admitted for permanent residence, or has otherwise been granted employment authorization by the United States Immigration and Naturalization Service.
(3) Have not been convicted of any felony crime within the ten-year period prior to the date of application.
(4) File application for the initial licensing and inspections of vehicles along with a list of all drivers who will be scheduled for driver permitting. An insurance binder must be provided for each vehicle to be used by the company.
(5) Submit the application fees.
(6) Provide the following information:
a. Name of business.
b. Physical address of the business.
c. Mailing address of the business.
d. Federal employer ID number or Social Security number.
e. The insignia (in color format), to be used on the vehicle.
f. Details of insurance coverage including agency, policy, and/or binder number, length of coverage, amounts and types of coverage.
g. The number of vehicles to be used.
h. Applicants full name, race, sex, nationality, Social Security number, alien registration number (if applicable), driver's license number, date of birth, home address, home phone number, mobile (cell) phone number, email address, and the amount of experience in the transportation of passengers.
i. Submit to a criminal background check.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1560:
(a) No certificate shall be issued unless there is in full force and effect liability insurance for each vehicle authorized for injury to any one person; in the amount of $1,000,000.00 for injuries to more than one person which are sustained in the same accident and $700,000.00 for property damage resulting from any one accident. Such liability insurance shall insure to the benefit of any person who shall be injured or who shall sustain damage to property caused by the negligence of a holder or his/her agents.
(b) Written documentation of the above stated insurance coverage, signed by an authorized agent of the insurer shall be filed in the office of the city clerk. Such insurance shall be carried with a company/agency authorized to do business in the State of Georgia.
(c) Each certificate of insurance submitted to the city clerk shall include, by endorsement to the policy, a statement that written notice shall be given to the city by certified mail, 30 days prior to cancellation or upon any material change in the coverage.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1561:
Any taxicab company operating under this article shall hold the city harmless against any and all liability, loss costs, damages, or expense, which may accrue, to the city by reason of the negligence of the holder. Nothing in this article shall be considered to make the city liable for damages because of any negligent act or omission or commission by any taxicab company, its drivers, or other employees, during the operation of a taxicab business or service, either in respect to injuries to person or with respect to damage to property which may be sustained.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1562:
Before an application will be considered for approval, a $200.00 application fee shall be paid. In the event the application is approved, the applicant will be responsible for paying the occupational tax license fee in accordance with the city's occupational tax license fee schedule. In the event that the application is denied, the city will retain $100.00 of the application fee to cover administrative costs associated with processing the application.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1563:
A certificate may be suspended or revoked by the city administrator, or his/her designee, for the following reasons:
(1) Furnishing fraudulent information requested in any application.
(2) Failure to pay all fees, or other charges imposed by this article.
(3) Failure to maintain all of the general qualifications applicable to the initial issuance of a certificate.
(4) Allowing the required insurance coverage to lapse.
(5) Violation of any provision of this article.
(6) Discontinuing operations for a period of more than 30 days, or failing to begin operations within 60 days of the date of issuance of the certificate.
Prior to any suspension or revocation, the certificate holder shall be given written notification at his/her last known address of the action, which shall include ground for such action.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1564:
(a) All certificates shall expire on December 31 of each year, including the year issued, but may be reinstated by the city administrator, or his/her designee, upon a renewal application being made and a determination that the applicant remains qualified as set forth in the ordinance, and upon payment of the appropriate fees.
(b) Certificates may be renewed only between November 15 and December 31 of each year for the following year. Certificates not renewed by December 31 shall be void and the certificate holder must re-apply as a new applicant in order to obtain a certificate.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1565:
It shall be unlawful for any person willfully to alter, deface or destroy a certificate of public convenience and necessity issued pursuant to this article.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1566:
(a) No automobile with less than four doors shall be operated as a taxicab on the streets of the city.
(b) The inside of all taxicabs shall be clean and free from liter.
(c) No taxicab shall be operated on the streets of the city which are in violation of O.C.G.A. § 40-8-7 which requires that all equipment be in good working order and safe mechanical condition.
(d) Each taxicab shall be equipped with an inside dome light which shall light up when the rear door is open and provide enough light so that the taxicab operator's permit may be clearly seen.
(e) Each taxicab shall be equipped with turn signals and brake lights.
(f) It shall be necessary for each taxicab to have a sign affixed on each side of the vehicle in accordance with regulations established by the city.
(g) The certificate number issued by the city shall be affixed to the two sides and the rear of each taxicab.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1567:
No person, firm, or corporation shall operate a taxicab on the city streets unless a taxicab operator's permit has been issued. All taxicabs shall display a current taxicab operator's permit issued by the city to signify compliance with this requirement.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1569:
The Cleveland Police Department shall conduct an investigation into the criminal history of each applicant for a taxicab operator's permit.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1570:
The initial application and permit fee is $235.00 plus any fees associated with the occupational tax ordinance. The annual permit and certificate renewal fee is $135.00 plus any fees associated with the occupational tax ordinance. Certificates not renewed by December 31 shall be void and the certificate holder must re-apply as a new applicant in order to obtain a certificate at a fee of $235.00 plus any fees associated with the occupational tax ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1571:
All persons driving taxicabs in the city shall be in good health and be capable of safely promoting the work of a taxicab driver.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1572:
(a) The city administrator or his/her designee shall upon consideration of the application approve or deny the taxicab operator's permit.
(b) The following shall be grounds for denial of permit:
(1) Failure to qualify under the criteria set forth in this article.
(2) A driver's history which contains more than five moving violations in the past five years.
(3) Current violation of any existing ordinance of the city.
(c) In the event that the permit is approved, the city administrator shall issue the permit to the applicant, the certificate holder.
(1) The permit is valid for the calendar year in which it was issued and shall expire on December 31 of each year unless renewed.
(2) The permit is nontransferable and is valid only for the driver while employed by the certificate holder named on the permit.
(3) The permit shall contain the name, company name and address, race, age, and photograph of the applicant.
(d) In the event the permit is denied, the city administrator or his/her designee shall notify the applicant in writing at his/her last known address with the reason for denial.

(1) To help make its decision, the city administrator or his/her designee shall take into consideration the number of existing taxicabs, whether existing transportation is adequate to meet the public need, the effect of this request on local traffic conditions, and the character, experience and responsibility of the applicant.
(2) The total number of taxicabs authorized under certificates issued shall not be greater than one vehicle per 1,000 residents of Cleveland, Georgia. Such population shall be based on the most current census information available from the Untied States Census Bureau.

1573:
A permit may be suspended or revoked by the city administrator for the following reasons:
(1) Failure to maintain all of the general qualifications applicable to the issuance of the permit;
(2) Violation of any provision of this article; or
(3) Violation of any traffic law while operating a taxicab.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1574:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a taxicab during any period in which such permit is suspended or revoked in accordance with the provisions of this article.

1575:
(a) All permits shall expire on December 31 of each year, including the year of issue, but may be reinstated by the city administrator, upon a renewal application being made and a determination that the applicant remains qualified as set forth in this article, and upon payment of the appropriate fees.

1576:
It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully alter, deface or destroy a taxicab operator's permit issued pursuant to this article.

1577:
(a) Every person to whom a taxicab operator's permit has been assigned shall return the permit to the city clerk upon discontinuing the operation of a taxicab for the certificate holder named on the permit. Such permit shall not be assigned or transferred to any other person or be valid for any other certificate holder. Permit holders who change employment shall apply to the city clerk's office for an updated permit that reflects the proper certificate holder for which the permitted will be employed.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any permit holder to allow his/her permit to be used by any other person.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1578:
Any and all licenses or permits granted pursuant to this article shall be subject to any future ordinances and regulations further regulating and governing the operation of taxicabs, or to additional and other regulations, or changing, modifying or withdrawing in whole or in part the approval or any privilege for the operation of such vehicles, as may in the judgment of the city council be consistent and to the best interest of the public welfare and safety.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1579:
Any person, firm, or corporation found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be punished as provided in section 16-75(c) of this Code.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, 4-9-2012)
1580:
(a) An applicant whose permit is denied or a permittee whose permit is suspended or revoked may request a hearing before the Cleveland City Council.
